established_findings.statement: Large language models (LLMs) have been applied to intent-to-configuration or natural-language-to-network-configuration tasks and can produce usable draft configurations under experimental conditions.
limitations: Many reported results are bench or emulation-based rather than large-scale production deployments.
Works report draft or candidate configurations; several note remaining syntax/semantic errors and need for verification or human oversight.
Evaluation datasets and task scopes vary across studies, limiting direct comparability and generalization.

established_findings.statement: Architectures that interpose deterministic verifiers or validators between stochastic generation and acceptance (generate–verify–repair / generate–validate–repair) have been proposed and empirically shown to increase detection and correction of mechanically verifiable defects.
limitations: Demonstrated improvements primarily address mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, compile/run failures, local policy violations); semantic correctness and broader operational safety remain challenging.
Some evaluations are single-case or limited-scale; human intervention or seeded repair context is still often required.

established_findings.statement: Deterministic network verification tools and formal-analysis approaches (e.g., Batfish, Plankton, header-space analysis, TLA+/SMT approaches) are mature methods for checking forwarding, reachability, and policy properties and are used as validators in research and practice.
limitations: Scalability, fidelity, and modelling trade-offs are recurrently noted (state explosion, protocol detail fidelity, topology changes).
Integration effort is required to use these tools as black-box validators for LLM outputs in heterogeneous operational environments.

established_findings.statement: LLM-only self-correction (without reliable external or deterministic feedback) is frequently unreliable; successful self-correction is typically observed only when dependable external feedback or verifiers are available or when tasks are especially self-monitorable.
limitations: Some task classes permit effective LLM self-correction, and large-scale fine-tuning or specialized pipelines can improve outcomes; conclusions depend on task taxonomy and available external signals.
Survey-level syntheses report mixed results across tasks and setups.

established_findings.statement: Prompt-injection and indirect prompt-injection are demonstrated, practical threats to LLM-integrated applications; proposed mitigations (filtering, detection classifiers, engineered defensive frameworks) can substantially reduce measured attack success rates in controlled evaluations.
limitations: Most mitigation evaluations are performed on curated adversarial corpora or synthetic attacks; real-world attack distributions and adaptive adversaries may differ.
Mitigations often trade off latency/usability and require continual updating against novel injection strategies.

established_findings.statement: Community work in 2023–2026 has produced multiple surveys, benchmarks, and prototype datasets for LLMs in NetOps and related evaluation methods, indicating active research but heterogeneous evaluation practices.
limitations: Available benchmarks and datasets differ in scope, format, and verification rigor; no single community-standard large-scale dataset covering intents, topologies, configs, and verifier-ground-truth is evident from these records.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do LLM-based configuration generators, when paired with deterministic verifiers, achieve operational readiness across diverse, large-scale production topologies and vendor heterogeneity?
limitations: Existing studies demonstrate feasibility on emulators, limited datasets, or single-case deployments; large-scale cross-vendor production evidence is not provided in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: How robust are proposed prompt-injection defenses and verifier-based pipelines against adaptive attackers who target NetOps-specific workflows (e.g., embedding malicious route/policy fragments inside retrieved artifacts)?
limitations: Records show defenses reduce success rates in controlled corpora; explicit NetOps-targeted adaptive-adversary evaluations are not present among supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: What standardized, verifiable evaluation metrics and datasets best capture operational correctness (intent satisfaction, safety, reachability constraints) for LLM-generated network configurations?
limitations: Several benchmarks and proposals exist but they vary in target properties; no consensus metric or unified dataset covering intents + verifiable ground truth appears in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: A publicly available, large-scale, standardized dataset that pairs operator natural-language intents with concrete topologies, vendor-specific configurations, and deterministic verifier-ground-truth results (for reachability/policy/assurance) is not evident in the supplied records and would address reproducibility and external-validity gaps.
limitations: Some benchmark efforts (NetConfEval, PreConfig, task-specific datasets) exist but do not collectively provide the full intent+topology+vendor+verifier-ground-truth combination at community scale based on the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirical evaluations of LLM+verifier pipelines under realistic sim-to-real domain shift (synthetic/emulated topologies → operational networks) are limited in the supplied set and represent a candidate research gap.
limitations: Records discuss sim/emulation usage and domain-shift concerns, but do not present large-scale sim-to-production transfer studies for LLM-driven NetOps in the supplied set.

candidate_gaps.statement: NetOps-specific adaptive adversary evaluations (prompt-injection vectors that exploit retrieval/tooling in intent-to-config pipelines) are underrepresented among the supplied threat/defense literature.
limitations: General prompt-injection and defenses are well-documented; targeted studies that combine NetOps pipelines, retrievals of operational artifacts, and adaptive adversaries are not present in the provided records.

excluded_claims: Claim: "LLM-based network configuration generators are production-ready and can be deployed without deterministic verification or human oversight." (Excluded — no supplied record provides production-scale evidence supporting this.)

Claim: "LLM self-correction reliably eliminates hallucinations for arbitrary NetOps tasks without external validators." (Excluded — surveys and empirical analyses in the records indicate self-correction is limited without reliable external feedback.)

Claim: "This work is the first to apply generate–verify–repair patterns to network configuration generation." (Excluded — multiple supplied records explicitly propose or evaluate GVR-like architectures in code and configuration domains.)

Claim: "Prompt-injection is a solved problem in NetOps contexts; existing defenses fully prevent operational compromise." (Excluded — supplied mitigation papers show substantial reductions in controlled tests but do not claim or demonstrate complete, adaptive-proof prevention in NetOps deployments.)
